# Threshold Reconciliation — Before / After

← [Back to README](../README.md)

Evidence: [`outputs/reports/threshold_reconciliation.json`](../outputs/reports/threshold_reconciliation.json)

**Threshold moved: 0.15333940006539568 → 0.17500000000000002**  
before: val, by F1-max (evaluation_report.json) — contaminated  
after: held-out slice of train (patient-level)

The contaminated value was fitted by F1-max on val, and val is also the
drift reference window — so the reference window carried a threshold
tuned to itself while the production window did not. The replacement is
selected on a held-out, patient-level slice of train.

Threshold optimism in the reported F1 drop: **0.0024**.

> **This number was itself corrected in Tier 2C.6.** Tier 2A.4 originally
> reported **0.0641**, which was an artifact: that block selected the
> threshold under one calibrator, then scored val under a second and test
> under a third. A threshold is a cut point on a probability scale, so
> comparing two windows on different calibrators is not a like-for-like
> comparison. Recomputed on a single scale, the optimism is small —
> **the val→test F1 degradation was largely real, not an artifact of a
> self-fitted threshold.** Found because this reconciliation produced a
> different test F1 than decontamination.json reported for the same
> threshold; the disagreement was the symptom.

changed and this comparison would not be interpretable.

## Subgroup disparity claims

The fairness audit does not report numbers so much as **claims** —
*this disparity is supported by the data*. Those are threshold-
dependent too, and one can be withdrawn without any headline number
moving.

Threshold 0.18000000000000002 → 0.17500000000000002

| Attribute | Metric | Change | Gap before | Gap after | Overlap now? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `age_band` | `recall` | **WITHDRAWN** | 0.1796 | 0.1717 | True |

Supported before: `{'race': ['ece'], 'gender': [], 'age_band': ['auc', 'recall', 'predicted_positive_rate']}`  
Supported after: `{'race': ['ece'], 'gender': [], 'age_band': ['auc', 'predicted_positive_rate']}`

## Interpretation

12 threshold-dependent values moved and no val→test direction reversed, so no degradation claim flips. BUT 1 SUBGROUP DISPARITY CLAIM(S) ARE WITHDRAWN: `age_band.recall`. At the corrected threshold those intervals overlap, so the disparity can no longer be distinguished from sampling noise. The gap did not vanish — the EVIDENCE for it did, and a claim that shipped as supported must now ship as not supported. A numbers-only diff would have missed this entirely, which is why the fairness audit is diffed at the level of what it CLAIMS rather than what it reports.
